notes.short: Living stones built into a spiritual house
notes.about: Peter carries one picture through these verses. Christ is the living stone, rejected by men, precious to God. Believers, like living stones, are built on Him into a spiritual house, a temple where they serve as a holy priesthood. To those who do not believe, the same stone is one they stumble over.

figure.name: Allegory
figure.words: like living stones, are being built into a spiritual house
figure.means: believers joined to Christ and to one another as a temple where God dwells and is worshiped, as He was in the temple of old

notes.evidence: John Calvin says calling believers living stones and a spiritual building sets them beside the ancient temple. Albert Barnes says Peter likens the church to the temple, with its own priesthood and sacrifices. Adam Clarke traces the bold metaphor until the living stones become one grand temple. A. J. Mason (Ellicott) says the language is figurative: the stones rise into a house of God.
notes.limit: The writers call it a comparison, a metaphor or a figure; none of them names it an allegory.

cites.quote: Peter no doubt meant to exhort the faithful to consecrate themselves as a spiritual temple to God ... By calling us living stones and spiritual building, as he had before said that Christ is a living stone, he intimates a comparison between us and the ancient temple; and this serves to amplify divine grace.

The purpose of the apostle here is to compare the church to a beautiful temple - such as the temple in Jerusalem, and to show that it is complete in all its parts, as that was. ... as in that there was a priesthood, and there were real and acceptable sacrifices offered, so it is in the Christian church.
cites.read: sacred-texts.com's transcription, in the copy at github.com/jonnyg23/mahabrain (commit b00aa50)

cites.quote: The metaphor in this and the following verse is as bold as it is singular ... Now, following the metaphor; these various living stones become one grand temple, in which God is worshipped, and in which he manifests himself as he did in the temple of old. Every stone - son and daughter, being a spiritual sacrificer or priest, they all offer up praise and thanksgiving to God through Christ
cites.read: sacred-texts.com's transcription, in the copy at github.com/jonnyg23/mahabrain (commit b00aa50)

cites.quote: The epithet is supplied, just as in “ living stone,” to make it abundantly clear that the language is figurative. ... here they are treated collectively (of course, along with the Gentile Christians), as so many stones, incomplete and unmeaning in themselves, by arrangement and cemented union to rise into an ideal house of God.

notes.short: The water of Noah's day pictures baptism
notes.about: In the ark eight people “were saved through water” (verse 20), and that water pictures “the baptism that now saves you also”. Peter adds that it is not a washing of the body but “the pledge of a clear conscience toward God”, and it saves through Christ's resurrection.

figure.name: Type
figure.words: this water symbolizes the baptism that now saves you also
figure.means: the flood water through which Noah's household was saved, a picture of Christian baptism, which saves through Christ's resurrection

original.note: In Peter's Greek “symbolizes” renders antitypon, the antitype, what answers to the earlier picture.

notes.evidence: Fausset (Jamieson, Fausset and Brown) calls the flood Noah's baptism and baptism its antitype, saving not of itself. Clarke sets the water that saved Noah beside the water of baptism. Mason (Ellicott's commentary) calls Noah's safe passage through the flood a type of baptism.
notes.limit: The verse itself says this is not the removal of dirt from the body. Two writers say the water does not save of itself: one ties it to repentance and faith, which it signs and seals, the other to the Spirit's renewing, which it pictures. Another sees in the flood a new beginning for mankind.

cites.quote: The flood was for Noah a baptism, as the passage through the Red Sea was for the Israelites … The antitypical water, namely, baptism, saves you also not of itself, nor the mere material water, but the spiritual thing conjoined with it, repentance and faith, of which it is the sign and seal
cites.read: sacred-texts.com's transcription, in the copy at github.com/jonnyg23/mahabrain (commit b00aa50)

cites.quote: Noah and his family were saved by water ... So the water of baptism, typifying the regenerating influence of the Holy Spirit, is the means of salvation to all those who receive this Holy Spirit in its quickening, cleansing efficacy. ... so the water of baptism saves no man, but as it is the means of his getting his heart purified by the Holy Spirit, and typifying to him that purification.

cites.quote: the water through which Noah was saved is said in the present day (“now,” as opposed to “in the days of Noe”) to save us … it foreshadowed something which does as a fact save us. … so Noe’s safe passage through the Flood is a type of baptism, because it was a regeneration of humanity
